How to properly connect PCIe cables to high power consumption graphics cards?

According to the power supply connector overuse definition from SilverStone warranty information. A single PCIe 8pin cable and connector’s maximum current rating is 12.5A, which is 150W (+12V x 12.5A). So SilverStone’s warranty will not cover damages or malfunction resulting from the use of a graphics card or expansion card with a single PCIe 8pin connector that exceeds standard 225W total power draw (150W from PCIe 8pin connector + 75W from PCIe motherboard slot). Similarly, a graphics card or expansion card with dual PCIe 8pin connectors that exceed 375W total power draw (300W from two PCIe 8pin connectors + 75W from PCIe motherboard slot) will also not be covered under warranty.

Thus, to power high consumption graphics cards (above 225W) with two or three PCIe slots, SilverStone recommends using two or three separate PCIe cables to connect such cards to the power supply.

My computer will trip the circuit breaker in my house, how do I prevent this?

If your computer is tripping the circuit breaker that means it is drawing too much power from one outlet. Please do the following： 

- Please make sure the computer is plugged directly into the wall outlet and do not use extension socket or other multiple outlet extension cords with the computer.
- If the use of extension socket is necessary, avoid combined usage with other higher powered household appliances such as TV, audio amplifier, etc… 
- Contact your local electrician for information on how you can upgrade your house to accommodate higher electrical draw.

5. How to correctly measure +12v value using a voltmeter?

 The OP and DA series PSUs have independent ground design that is separate from +5V and +3.3V ground. So when you use voltmeter to measure +12V and connect ground to +5V or +3.3V ground, the circuit is incomplete and the voltmeter will report the wrong value. If you properly connect the voltmeter to +12V and +12V’s ground, the correct value should be detected. Please see attached picture for reference.

When pressing the system's power button, both green and red LED glow and the system does not start.

| 1.) | The ST30NF and ST45NF are based off of server platform designs so they have very sensitive auto-protection mechanisms. If the system you are using has minor shorting or other faults, ST30NF/ST45NF’s auto-protection will trigger and shuts off the power supply (green + red LED). |
| --- | --- |
| 2.) | Amber + green LED indicates that the ST30NF is in standby mode and waiting for action (if you turn on your system, both LED will turn green if there is no problem). |
| 3.) | Green + Red LED can also indicates that the PSU itself has a problem or auto-protection is triggered. You should not have Amber + Green LED in standby mode and 2x Green LED without connected to the system. |
| How to check and find possible faults: | |
| - | Please first check, if all connectors are correct and firmly attached. Please unplug them and plug in again, to make sure that they have correct and good connection. |
| - | Please check your system for any items that can cause a shortage (for example a missing screw on the motherboard from installation wedged between the component and case) |
| - | Check if any of your drives is causing the problem. You can try dismounting all drives from the power supply to see if the system can start. You can also do this with your expansion cards, memory, etc… Uninstall the extension cards or other parts and check if the system starts. |
| - | Sometimes mounting bracket from the CPU cooler can cause a short if it comes in contact against a condenser or MOSFET. The CPU cooler bracket at the rear side of the motherboard may not be insulated well and cause a short there. |
| - | If possible, check the ST30NF in another working system. |

How to properly connect PCIe cables to high power consumption graphics cards?

According to the power supply connector overuse definition from SilverStone warranty information. A single PCIe 8pin cable and connector’s maximum current rating is 12.5A, which is 150W (+12V x 12.5A). So SilverStone’s warranty will not cover damages or malfunction resulting from the use of a graphics card or expansion card with a single PCIe 8pin connector that exceeds standard 225W total power draw (150W from PCIe 8pin connector + 75W from PCIe motherboard slot). Similarly, a graphics card or expansion card with dual PCIe 8pin connectors that exceed 375W total power draw (300W from two PCIe 8pin connectors + 75W from PCIe motherboard slot) will also not be covered under warranty.

Thus, to power high consumption graphics cards (above 225W) with two or three PCIe slots, SilverStone recommends using two or three separate PCIe cables to connect such cards to the power supply.
